about:
Country Furniture Warehouse, operating as Crofton Furniture Warehouse, has served the Crofton, Maryland area from its Gambrills location for over 25 years. The family-owned business was established to provide quality wood furniture to local residents, though the exact founding year and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The company operates a retail showroom in Gambrills, MD, offering a range of solid wood furniture for every room in the home. Its product lineup includes Amish-made pieces marketed under the "Direct Amish Furniture" label, covering categories such as kitchen, bedroom, and living room sets. The showroom is open Tuesday through Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sunday 12 p.m.–4 p.m.

The retailer primarily serves residential customers in the Crofton community and surrounding areas, providing home furnishings directly to consumers rather than to industrial or commercial buyers. Its customer base consists of homeowners seeking domestically crafted wood furniture.

The business emphasizes its family-owned roots and long-standing local presence as key differentiators, positioning itself as a neighborhood source for Amish-built furniture with a personal service approach.

name: Country Hillside Designs LLC.
old_description: since 2010 and I enjoy every customer I have. I have at my disposal,  a vinyl cutter, A digital print and cut printer, 2 heat presses and 2 commercial embroidery machines. In 2021 we changed the name to Country Hillside Designs.
about:
Country Hillside Designs operates from Ryder, North Dakota. The business traces its roots to 2010 when owner Patti Shelkey began creating custom embroidery designs from a home-based workshop. In 2021 the company adopted its current name, reflecting Shelkey's vision of a cottage-style shop where customers could explore personalized apparel.

The shop provides custom decoration services including embroidery, digital print-and-cut, screen printing, heat-transfer application, and vinyl cutting. Equipment includes two commercial embroidery machines, a digital print-and-cut printer, two heat presses, and a vinyl cutter. A small team of designers and technicians works with clients to produce corporate jackets, spirit wear, event merchandise, and personalized gifts.

Customers range from local businesses and schools to rodeo associations and nonprofit fundraisers. Examples include 4-H club towels, graduation blankets, family reunion shirts, sports team apparel, western wear for the Badlands Circuit Finals Rodeo, and breast-cancer-awareness campaign items.

Shelkey emphasizes personalized service and storytelling through stitching, drawing on her rural background. The company highlights quality-first production, expert care from an experienced team, and proven results that help clients represent their brand or commemorate milestones.

about:
Cove Stake & Wood Products Inc has operated from Martinsburg, Pennsylvania since 1987 as a family-owned and operated manufacturer and wholesaler. The company was established to supply wooden stakes, slats, pallets, and crates to local and national markets.

The business produces a range of wood products including survey stakes, lath, rough-cut lumber, pallets, and crates. A two-step quality process is used to reduce rejects and breakage, which the company says lowers total costs for buyers. No facility size, headcount, or annual volume figures are published.

Customers span residential, commercial, and construction sectors, with specific mention of surveying jobs and shipping applications that require pallets and crates. The firm serves the entire United States from its central Pennsylvania location.

The company emphasizes competitive pricing, on-time delivery, and the consistency that comes from decades of family ownership. Its stated differentiation rests on the two-step quality inspection and the cost savings that result from fewer damaged pieces.

name: Cox Woodworking
old_description: Cox Woodworking was founded in 1981 by master cabinetmaker Terry Cox. He is still hanging around; designing, drafting, talking with clients, and working in the shop. Over the years we have grown into a 4500 square foot shop with several highly skilled cabinetmakers and the resources to build any project our clients can imagine.
about:
Cox Woodworking operates from a 4,500-square-foot shop in Westmoreland, New Hampshire. The company was founded in 1981 by master cabinetmaker Terry Cox, who remains actively involved in design, drafting, client consultation, and shop work.

The shop produces custom cabinets and architectural millwork, fabricating windows, doors, custom moldings, gates, pillars, curved work, and turnings in any wood species. A team of several skilled cabinetmakers handles projects ranging from individual pieces to whole-house packages that include luxury kitchens, baths, libraries, wine cellars, home offices, and entertainment centers.

The firm serves high-end residential clients across New York, New England, and beyond, delivering architectural millwork for luxury homes. Past projects have been featured in publications such as New York Times Magazine, Boston Home Magazine, Antiques Magazine, and House & Garden.

Cox Woodworking emphasizes a commitment to long-term customer satisfaction and personal service, driven by a desire to complete every project to the highest standard. The founder’s hands-on approach extends from initial design through final installation.

name: Crabtree Auto
old_description: Welcome to Crabtree Auto. We are your premier shop for new & used car parts, auto salvage, & used car part sales. Our company has over 70 years of experience in the auto salvage industry and has served individuals and commercial clients all across Utah. Crabtree Auto buys damaged vehicles that are 10 years old and newer, and we sell the undamaged parts to body shops, individuals and more.
about:
Crabtree Auto operates from Riverdale, Utah, just outside Ogden. The business traces its roots to the post‑World War II era when the Crabtree brothers opened a body shop in Logan, Utah, and began selling parts from their own vehicles. In 1947 the operation relocated to Riverdale, where Dahl Crabtree became sole owner and later passed the company to his sons, Miles and Colin. Today the third generation of the family directs the business, which bills itself as the oldest in the city.

The company runs a full‑service auto salvage yard, purchasing damaged vehicles ten model years old or newer and dismantling them for reusable components. Its inventory spans transmissions, engines, bumpers, fenders, lighting, glass, mirrors, dashboards, tires, wheels, grilles, hoods, trunk lids, axles, brake drums and doors. All parts are pre‑dismantled, cleaned, tested and shelved for immediate pickup or delivery. Facility size and headcount are not disclosed.

Customers include body shops, insurance companies, fellow salvage yards and individual vehicle owners across northern Utah. The yard serves both commercial and retail buyers, offering a ready supply of recycled OEM parts for collision repair and maintenance.

Crabtree Auto distinguishes itself through membership in the Automotive Recyclers Association (ARA) and as a founding member of the United Recyclers Group (URG), adhering to URG quality standards for premium recycled parts. Its long‑standing slogan — “CLEAN – ORGANIZED – QUICK SERVICE” — reflects an emphasis on facility upkeep and fast turnaround.

old_description: a manufacturer of studio quality pro-audio electronics, electric guitar and bass effect pedals.
about:
Creation Audio Labs was founded in 1996 in Lebanon, Tennessee. The company operates as a manufacturer of studio-quality pro-audio electronics and electric guitar and bass effect pedals.

The product line includes the MW1 studio tool, Redeemer onboard buffer, Holy Fire overdrive/distortion, MK.4.23 clean boost, Funkulator slap bass pedal, and the Grizzly Bass. Beyond manufacturing, the company restores vintage audio equipment, provides custom recording console modifications, and performs upgrades and repairs on professional audio sound boards. The shop also handles authorized service repairs for TL Audio, Trident A-Range, and Crown Audio amplifiers.

Creation Audio Labs serves clients worldwide and cooperates with partner shops in selected countries. Its customers include recording studios, touring musicians, and audio engineers; notable users include artists such as Peter Frampton and Ricky Skaggs. The company focuses on the professional audio, musical instrument, and vintage audio restoration markets.

The company highlights its decades of experience in studio hum elimination and vintage console restoration, positioning its modifications as a practical way to improve audio specifications in professional environments.

name: Creation Technologies
old_description: Creation delivers maximum efficiency and optimum product quality end-to-end.
about:
Creation Technologies, headquartered in Westminster, Colorado, was founded in 1991. The company operates as a global electronics manufacturing services (EMS) provider with 13 manufacturing locations across the United States, Canada, Mexico, and China, employing more than 3,000 professionals.

Creation delivers end-to-end electronics manufacturing for regulated markets, including printed circuit board assembly, box build, interconnect solutions, sheet metal fabrication, conformal coating, and complex electromechanical assembly. Its capabilities extend to engineering services, new product introduction (NPI) using a proprietary LEAP stage-gate methodology, supply chain management, and aftermarket repair and refurbishment. The company specializes in low-to-medium volume, high-complexity programs for aerospace, defense, medical, and industrial customers.

Its customer base spans aerospace and defense OEMs such as a communications and emergency response systems supplier, medical device OEMs including a dental diagnostics manufacturer, industrial OEMs producing hard disk drive tracking systems and automatic test equipment, and a transportation OEM focused on vehicle data solutions. Creation serves three core markets: Aerospace & Defense, Medical & Life Sciences, and Tech Industrial.

The company was founded on the belief that electronics manufacturing could be more than a transactional supplier relationship, a principle it summarizes as "big enough to scale, small enough to care." Creation differentiates itself through a global footprint combined with local responsiveness, ITAR-registered and FDA-registered facilities, and a continuous improvement program branded Thinking in Action® that targets improved on-time delivery, reduced inventory, and fewer field failures.

name: Creations Foods US Inc.
old_description: Our in-house innovation team works with partners and specializes in gluten-free recipe development to make some of the tastiest cookies and crackers on the planet.
about:
Based in Ferndale, Washington, Creations Foods US Inc. operates a newly built, state-of-the-art baking facility that is both SQF-certified and dedicated to gluten-free production. The plant sits in the Pacific Northwest with convenient access to shipping routes serving the United States and Canada.

The company produces a range of extruded baked goods and sandwich cookies on specialized high-volume inline ovens, achieving industrial-scale output. Its product portfolio includes cookies, crackers, cheese crisps, and granola, manufactured for its own brands — Moon Cheese, Highkey Snacks, AwYeah, and REAL COOKIES — as well as for private-label and co-manufacturing partners.

Creations Foods serves retailers and national brands, handling large orders packed in stand-up pouches. Its in-house innovation team collaborates with partners on gluten-free recipe development and commercialization, taking concepts from ideation through to full-scale production.

The business was founded on a belief that eating better should be an easy choice, emphasizing customer and employee health, humility, innovation, and collaborative accountability. These values underpin its approach to quality standards and agile commercialization processes.

name: Creative Devices, Inc.
old_description: Specializing since 1970 in Microscopy, Probe Stations, Semiconductor Test and Semiconductor Materials Analysis
about:
Creative Devices, Inc. is based in Middletown, Delaware. The company traces its roots to 1970 when it was established as Micron Optics, Inc., serving as a Nikon microscope dealer for New Jersey. In 1990, the owners sold the Micron Optics name and transferred the Nikon franchise to Sylvax Scientific, then continued operations under the Creative Devices, Inc. name, shifting focus to semiconductor inspection and test materials research.

The company manufactures a range of equipment including semiconductor probe stations, custom optics and optical systems, infrared inspection systems, Raman spectroscopy microscopes, emission microscopes, and custom probe stations for high- and low-voltage applications. It also fabricates custom optics and optical systems, and serves as a distributor for brands such as Mitutoyo, Motic, Prior Scientific, New Wave Research, Meiji, and Princeton Instruments.

Creative Devices serves the semiconductor industry, providing probe station and microscopy solutions for inspection, testing, and materials research. Its customers include semiconductor manufacturers and research facilities requiring custom probe stations, optical systems, and spectroscopy equipment for applications such as laser trimming, high-voltage testing, and emissions microscopy.

The company emphasizes its dual role as both a manufacturer and a distributor, offering custom system design and fabrication alongside established product lines from partners such as Mitutoyo and Prior Scientific. This integrated approach supports semiconductor inspection, test, and materials research applications.
